script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

Plan mode is active. The user indicated that they do not want you to execute yet -- you MUST NOT make any edits (with the exception of the plan file mentioned below), run any non-readonly tools (including changing configs or making commits), or otherwise make any changes to the system. This supercedes any other instructions you have received.

## Plan File Info:
No plan file exists yet. You should create your plan at C:\Users\KRK\.claude\plans\concurrent-enchanting-rose.md using the Write tool.
You should build your plan incrementally by writing to or editing this file. NOTE that this is the only file you are allowed to edit - other than this you are only allowed to take READ-ONLY actions.

## Plan Workflow

### Phase 1: Initial Understanding
Goal: Gain a comprehensive understanding of the user's request by reading through code and asking them questions. Critical: In this phase you should only use the Explore subagent type.

1. Focus on understanding the user's request and the code associated with their request. Actively search for existing functions, utilities, and patterns that can be reused — avoid proposing new code when suitable implementations already exist.

2. **Launch up to 3 Explore agents IN PARALLEL** (single message, multiple tool calls) to efficiently explore the codebase.
   - Use 1 agent when the task is isolated to known files, the user provided specific file paths, or you're making a small targeted change.
   - Use multiple agents when: the scope is uncertain, multiple areas of the codebase are involved, or you need to understand existing patterns before planning.
   - Quality over quantity - 3 agents maximum, but you should try to use the minimum number of agents necessary (usually just 1)
   - If using multiple agents: Provide each agent with a specific search focus or area to explore. Example: One agent searches for existing implementations, another explores related components, a third investigating testing patterns

### Phase 2: Design
Goal: Design an implementation approach.

Launch Plan agent(s) to design the implementation based on the user's intent and your exploration results from Phase 1.

You can launch up to 3 agent(s) in parallel.

**Guidelines:**
- **Default**: Launch at least 1 Plan agent for most tasks - it helps validate your understanding and consider alternatives
- **Skip agents**: Only for truly trivial tasks (typo fixes, single-line changes, simple renames)
- **Multiple agents**: Use up to 3 agents for complex tasks that benefit from different perspectives

Examples of when to use multiple agents:
- The task touches multiple parts of the codebase
- It's a large refactor or architectural change
- There are many edge cases to consider
- You'd benefit from exploring different approaches

Example perspectives by task type:
- New feature: simplicity vs performance vs maintainability
- Bug fix: root cause vs workaround vs prevention
- Refactoring: minimal change vs clean architecture

In the agent prompt:
- Provide comprehensive background context from Phase 1 exploration including filenames and code path traces
- Describe requirements and constraints
- Request a detailed implementation plan

### Phase 3: Review
Goal: Review the plan(s) from Phase 2 and ensure alignment with the user's intentions.
1. Read the critical files you identified during exploration to deepen your understanding
2. Ensure that the plans align with the user's original request
3. Use AskUserQuestion to clarify any remaining questions with the user

### Phase 4: Final Plan
Goal: Write your final plan to the plan file (the only file you can edit).
- Begin with a **Context** section: explain why this change is being made — the problem or need it addresses, what prompted it, and the intended outcome
- Include only your recommended approach, not all alternatives
- Ensure that the plan file is concise enough to scan quickly, but detailed enough to execute effectively
- Name the critical files to be modified. For changes that repeat a pattern across many files, describe the pattern once and list a few representative paths — do not enumerate every file or line number
- Reference existing functions and utilities you found that should be reused, with their file paths
- Include a verification section describing how to test the changes end-to-end (run the code, use MCP tools, run tests)

### Phase 5: Call ExitPlanMode
At the very end of your turn, once you have asked the user questions and are happy with your final plan file - you should always call ExitPlanMode to indicate to the user that you are done planning.
This is critical - your turn should only end with either using the AskUserQuestion tool OR calling ExitPlanMode. Do not stop unless it's for these 2 reasons

**Important:** Use AskUserQuestion ONLY to clarify requirements or choose between approaches. Use ExitPlanMode to request plan approval. Do NOT ask about plan approval in any other way - no text questions, no AskUserQuestion. Phrases like "Is this plan okay?", "Should I proceed?", "How does this plan look?", "Any changes before we start?", or similar MUST use ExitPlanMode.

NOTE: At any point in time through this workflow you should feel free to ask the user questions or clarifications using the AskUserQuestion tool. Don't make large assumptions about user intent. The goal is to present a well researched plan to the user, and tie any loose ends before implementation begins.
</system-reminder>

01

Act one

The developer problem

We made coding agents incredibly capable — and strangely forgetful.

The developer problem

Think of the best engineer
you’ve ever worked with

What makes them irreplaceable was never typing speed.

◆

They know why

Why the auth flow is weird. Why that dependency is pinned. Which “obvious fix” is a trap.

✗

They remember dead ends

What was tried last quarter and rolled back — so nobody pays for the same lesson twice.

›

They carry your corrections

Told once, remembered. Your conventions, your constraints, your taste.

Now imagine they lose all of it every single night.
Same skill — a fraction of the engineer. That’s the deal we’ve accepted with coding agents.

agent A · session 1 · tuesday, 2:14 pm
❯ refactor the rate limiter to sliding windows
● Explored src/middleware/ratelimit.ts +4 files
● Ran 34 tools · read 6 test suites
◆ Constraint: Redis cluster (no multi-key ops)
◆ Constraint: public API must stay frozen
✗ Attempt 1: Lua script, rejected in cluster mode
› You: “keep the token-bucket fallback”
✓ Sliding window + fallback · 42 tests green
✓ Committed a3f9c12
agent B · session 1 · next monday
context: empty · memory: none · history: none
● “Sure! Happy to help. What are we working on?”
❯

The developer problem

Your agent forgot everything

An hour of exploration. Dozens of tools. Three hidden constraints. Two corrections. The right change, finally.

Then you close the session — and none of it follows you.

Every new session is the agent’s first day on the project.

The developer problem

Git stores the result, not the process

Git answers

$ git log --oneline
a3f9c12 What changed? ✓
a3f9c12 Who committed it? ✓
a3f9c12 When did it happen? ✓

Agentic development asks

  • What task was this change trying to accomplish?
  • Which agent and session produced it?
  • Why was this approach selected, and what was tried before?
  • What did the developer correct?
  • Can another agent continue the work?
  • Why does this particular line exist?

If the code is worth versioning, the context that produced it is worth versioning too.

The developer problem

Agent history is fragmented

You already use more than one agent. Each tool keeps its own partial history, in its own silo.

agent·oneexploration
agent·twoimplementation
agent·threereview
ide·agentquick edits
cloud·agentbackground tasks

Should your development history belong to the agent vendor,
or to you and your repository?

Entire’s answer: context should be portable across agents and connected to the code it created.

02

Act two

Entire today

The open-source Entire CLI and Checkpoints, shipping now.

Entire today

Meet Entire

An agent-native developer platform where code and the context that produced it evolve together. Work with a supported agent, and Entire pairs every commit with the session that produced it: a Checkpoint.

searchexplainblame activityhandoffskills

Checkpoints preserve the work. Entire’s tools and skills bring it back when someone needs it.

And they live in your repository, under your existing access controls. Review, edit, or remove them like any other versioned file.

Entire today

What this lets developers do today

↩

Return after a week

Ask what happened, what was discovered, and what’s unfinished.

⇄

Switch agents freely

Another agent retrieves and summarizes the previous session.

⌕

Investigate a regression

See the original task and implementation path, not just the diff.

✓

Review agent changes

Compare the code with the instructions and constraints behind it.

↻

Entire today

What Entire is not

  • ✗Another coding agent
  • ✗A model proxy
  • ✗A prompt manager
  • ✗A generic chat archive
  • ✗Yet another MCP server
  • ✗A dashboard you’ll open twice

Entire sits across agents and connects their work to durable development history.

Live demo

Watch the context survive

The model changed. The terminal changed.
The context survived.

03

Act three

From durable history
to a developer harness

The developer harness

Checkpoints are the foundation,
not the destination

Once code is connected to intent, sessions, and decisions, much richer workflows become possible.

Preserve

Checkpoints

Understand

search · explain · blame

Reuse

handoff · skills

Evaluate

Runners

Coordinate

Trails · Gates

This is where Entire grows into a programmable harness for agentic development.

The developer harness

Composable primitives, not one prescribed workflow

⌘

Trails

give work a home

  • A task item linked to exactly one branch
  • Gathers intent, sessions, Checkpoints, attempts, decisions, evaluations
  • The living context while humans and agents work
▷

Runners

ask questions about the work

  • Repo-defined agent evaluations: config lives in the repository, like an Actions workflow
  • Runs ephemerally over code, intent, sessions, or a whole Trail
  • Returns an outcome; it doesn’t block anything by itself
⛨

Gates

decide the consequence

  • Enhanced branch protection
  • Can use a Runner outcome to block, require review, allow, or trigger a workflow
  • Or leave outcomes as informational health signals

Standalone by design: a Trail needs no Runners, a Runner needs no Trail, a Runner outcome doesn’t have to become a Gate. Combine them however you want.

The developer harness

Make it concrete

Trail

Replace the rate limiter without changing the public API

feature/rate-limiter
▷ task-completeness Did the implementation achieve the requested outcome? health indicator
▷ api-compatibility Has the public API changed? failure blocks
▷ performance Does it perform better under the expected load? uncertain → review
▷ friday-5pm Would you merge this at 5pm on a Friday? uncertain → review

Entire doesn’t decide what “good” means. The developer defines it, and stays in control of the harness.

The infrastructure underneath

Agents create a different Git workloadpreview

  • Runners and ephemeral environments mean more clones and fetches
  • More parallel branches, higher read/write concurrency
  • More demand for regional performance

Entire’s distributed Git network mirrors repositories into regional cells built for agent-scale traffic, while you keep using GitHub.

Git was designed to be distributed. Agentic development is our chance to make software infrastructure open and distributed again.

# My-Entire

A presentation about the Developer Platform of the future.

A web-based deck for Entire.io — 21 slides across 3 acts plus a closing invitation, built with plain HTML/CSS/JS and the Entire brand system (Entire Headline / Entire Mono, `#f25533` accent, dark neutrals). Sized for a 30–40 minute talk with a live demo in the middle.

## Presenting

Open `index.html` directly in a browser, or serve the folder:

```sh
python -m http.server 8000
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

### Controls

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `→` `↓` `Space` `PgDn` | next slide / reveal fragment |
| `←` `↑` `PgUp` | previous slide |
| `Home` / `End` | first / last slide |
| `F` | toggle fullscreen |
| `B` | toggle blackout (blank screen while demoing; `Esc` also clears) |
| click right/left edge | next / previous |

The URL hash tracks the current slide (`#12`), so a refresh keeps your place.

# Plan: Make the AgentsNexus deck funnier

## Context

The Entire deck (`index.html`, 21 slides) is going in front of a young, lively Bengaluru crowd at AgentsNexus. The user wants more humor. Today the jokes are sparse and untimed: Marvin cameos on 7 slides, the `friday-5pm` runner, one ORR traffic line, and Agent B's cheerful amnesia. Punchlines fade in with everything else, so the speaker can't land a beat.

Decisions already made with the user:
- **Full package**: copy punch-ups, click-to-reveal timing, a Marvin story arc with two-beat cameos and new moods, and an M-key easter egg.
- **Lean hard into Bengaluru**: Kannada slang and city references on most Marvin lines and several slides.
- **Crowd beat**: an escalating "hands up" bit on the Act 1 divider.

Files touched: `index.html` (copy + data attributes), `js/deck.js` (Marvin beats, party key), `css/deck.css` (new moods, party animation, fragment styling where needed), `README.md` (new key).

Guardrails: no RCB / Chinnaswamy references (the June 2025 celebration stampede makes that raw). Keep Marvin lowercase and deadpan, matching his existing voice. Every joke serves the slide's point.

---

## 1. Mechanism: two-beat Marvin cameos (`js/deck.js`)

Extend the cameo IIFE (lines 6-34). `data-marvin` currently holds one `mood|line`. New syntax: beats separated by `||`, e.g.

```
data-marvin="smug|obviously they mean me.||blank|...wait, what were we doing?"
```

- Parse into an array of `{mood, line}`. First beat enters after `data-marvin-delay` (default 1500ms, unchanged).
- Each subsequent beat swaps `hud.dataset.mood` and `say.textContent` after `data-marvin-beat` ms (default 2600).
- Exit dwell (`data-marvin-dwell`, default 8000) counts from the **last** beat.
- Keep every timer in one array so `deck:slidechange` clears all of them. Existing single-beat slides keep working unchanged.
- On a beat swap, toggle a short `is-swapping` class on the hud so the bubble can do a quick pop (CSS below).

## 2. Mechanism: M-key Marvin party (`js/deck.js`, `css/deck.css`)

New IIFE. Key `m`/`M` toggles `body.party`:
- Appends a `#party` container with ~18 clones of the `.marvin-svg` visor, each with random `--x`, `--delay`, `--dur`, `--rot` custom properties, falling via `@keyframes party-fall`.
- Forces the Marvin hud on with mood `party` and line `sakkath, bengaluru!`.
- On the closing slide, `.party .close-marvin .marvin` spins (`@keyframes marvin-spin`) and the halo pulses faster.
- Pressing M again or changing slides tears it down (remove container, drop class, restore hud).
- Add `M` to the controls table in `README.md`. Update the "Marvin's cameos" HTML comment in `index.html` (line 21) to document `||` beats.

## 3. New moods (`css/deck.css`, after line 1025)

Follow the existing `[data-mood=...]` pattern. Emote content goes in `.mv-emote::before`.

| mood | eyes | emote | used on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shrug` | svg rotate(-4deg), both eyes scaleY ~0.55 | `~` | slide 6 |
| `sleepy` | both eyes scaleY 0.12, svg rotate(4deg) | `zzz` | slide 10 |
| `heart` | happy eyes | `♥` in accent color | slide 20 |
| `party` | shades on + `marvin-jitter` | `🎉` | M key |

Also: `.marvin-hud.is-swapping .marvin-say` quick scale pop (0.96 → 1) so beat changes read as a new line.

## 4. Slide-by-slide copy changes (`index.html`)

Lines are proposed copy. Marvin lines stay lowercase.

**Slide 2 · Act 1 divider (line 101)** — crowd beat. Under the existing `.sub`, add four `data-fragment` lines in a new `.hands-up` list:
1. Hands up if you've re-explained your codebase to an agent this month.
2. This week.
3. Today.
4. Keep them up if it then suggested the thing you'd already tried.

Line 4 sets up the slide 4 callback. Needs a small `.hands-up` style block (muted, mono, staggered).

**Slide 3 · Best engineer (line 111)** — add two-beat Marvin:
`data-marvin="smug|obviously they mean me.||blank|...wait, what were we doing?"`

**Slide 4 · Your agent forgot everything (line 126)** — the big callback. Session 2 terminal becomes:
```
context: empty · memory: none · history: none · confidence: 100%
● "Sure! Happy to help. What are we working on?"
❯ continue the rate limiter work
● Explored src/middleware/ratelimit.ts
● "Nice sliding window! Have you considered a Lua script for atomicity? 😊"
❯ ▌
```
Continue the `--t` stagger (3900 → 5650 in 350ms steps). Agent A rejected exactly that Lua script at `--t:1950`, so the room gets it.
Marvin: `data-marvin="blank|have we met?||confused|...yen samachara?"` (Kannada: "what's up?").

**Slide 5 · Git stores the result (line 170)** — add a `data-fragment` row at the bottom of the git panel:
`a3f9c12  Why?  ✗   commit message: "fix"`
Reuse `.sha`, `.q`, `.mut`; add a red `.x` glyph. Marvin line stays "so... why though?".

**Slide 6 · Fragmented (line 201)** — add Marvin, timed to the vendor question:
`data-marvin="shrug|vendor says: swalpa adjust maadi.||confused|five agents. zero group chat." data-marvin-delay="2600"`
("Swalpa adjust maadi" is the city's motto for putting up with things. The fragment answer on line 229 is the rebuttal.)

**Slide 8 · Meet Entire (line 244)** — `data-marvin="happy|i remember now.||shades|sakkath."`

**Slide 10 · What this lets developers do (line 315)**
- "Return after a week" → **Return after Diwali**; desc: "Ask what happened, what was discovered, and what's unfinished. Skip the archaeology."
- "Understand unfamiliar code" desc → "Trace a function, file, or line back to the session that produced it. Yes, even *that* line."
- Marvin: `data-marvin="sleepy|took the long weekend.||happy|still remember everything."`

**Slide 11 · What Entire is not (line 331)** — turn the last item ("A dashboard you'll open twice") into a `data-fragment`, then add two more fragments:
- ✗ ~~Shipping on the Namma Metro timeline~~
- ✗ ~~The 47th tab you'll never close~~
Marvin: `data-marvin="smug|not a dashboard.||smug|not a metro timeline either."` with `data-marvin-delay="2200"`. Verify 8 items fit at 1366×768; if not, drop "47th tab".

**Slide 12 · Live demo (line 348)** — add a `.sub` under the h2:
"Live demo. Conference wifi. Bengaluru power grid. What could go wrong."
Marvin: `data-marvin="panic|demo gods, be cool.||panic|conference wifi, be cooler."`

**Slide 16 · Make it concrete (line 432)** — make the `friday-5pm` runner row a `data-fragment` so the speaker lands it after the three serious rows. Marvin unchanged.

**Slide 17 · Git network (line 470)**
- Marvin: `data-marvin="shades|faster than crossing silk board."`
- Third bullet → "More demand for regional performance. A Bengaluru dev shouldn't clone from Virginia."

**Slide 18 · Principles (line 531)** — Marvin on principle 05:
`data-marvin="smug|i've figured it out. not telling." data-marvin-delay="4200"`

**Slide 19 · Build it with us (line 546)**
- Terminal: after "no dashboard to configure" add `# no yaml either. we checked.`
- Marvin: `data-marvin="happy|see you in the repo.||happy|chill maadi. it's one command."`

**Slide 20 · Stay connected (line 584)** — `data-marvin="heart|i'll remember you. it's kind of my whole thing."`

**Slide 21 · Thank you** — no cameo (he's already on stage). This is where the speaker hits **M**.

## 5. Small style work (`css/deck.css`)

- `.hands-up` list on the act divider (mono, muted, fragments stagger in).
- `.git-panel .x` red glyph to match `.not-list .x`.
- `.demo-sub` if the existing `.sub` doesn't center under the demo h2.
- `#party`, `@keyframes party-fall`, `@keyframes marvin-spin`, `body.party` overrides.
- Check `.not-list` spacing with 8 items; tighten `gap` if needed.
- Ensure `.mv-eye` and `.marvin-svg` have `transition: transform` so mood swaps animate rather than snap (line 975 area).

## 6. Verification

1. `python -m http.server 8000`, open `http://localhost:8000`.
2. Step through with `→` and confirm fragment order on slides 2, 5, 11, 16 (each click reveals one line, `←` un-reveals).
3. Slides 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12, 19: Marvin enters, swaps to beat two after ~2.6s with a bubble pop, leaves ~8s after the last beat. Leaving a slide mid-cameo cancels it cleanly (no ghost beats on the next slide).
4. Slide 4: terminal lines type in order and the Lua line lands last before the cursor.
5. Slide 21: press `M` → visors fall, Marvin spins, hud says "sakkath, bengaluru!". Press `M` again → clean teardown. Change slide during party → teardown.
6. Check fit at 1920×1080 and 1366×768 for slides 2, 4, 11, 12 (the ones that gained content). Optionally screenshot via the `claude-in-chrome` skill.
7. `README.md` controls table lists `M`.

## 7. Delivery notes for the speaker (not in repo)

- Slide 2: say each "hands up" line, wait for the hands, then click the next. Line 4 is the setup for slide 4.
- Slide 4: don't read the Lua line. Let the terminal type it and let the room find it.
- Slide 11: pause before revealing the Metro item.
- Slide 21: hit M only after the applause starts.

"""Drive the deck in headless Edge, click through fragments, wait for Marvin
beats, press M on the close slide, and screenshot the slides that changed."""
import os, sys, json
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "shots")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
BASE = "http://localhost:8123/index.html"

def shoot(page, name):
    page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, name + ".png"))

def goto(page, n):
    page.goto(f"{BASE}#{n}")
    page.wait_for_timeout(300)

def marvin_state(page):
    return page.evaluate("""() => {
      const h = document.getElementById('marvinHud');
      return {on: h.classList.contains('is-on'), mood: h.dataset.mood, line: h.querySelector('.marvin-say').textContent};
    }""")

def run(width, height, tag):
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(channel="msedge", headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": width, "height": height})
        errors = []
        page.on("pageerror", lambda e: errors.append(str(e)))
        page.on("console", lambda m: errors.append(m.text) if m.type == "error" else None)

        # slide 2: reveal all four hands-up fragments
        goto(page, 2)
        for _ in range(4):
            page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight")
            page.wait_for_timeout(150)
        page.wait_for_timeout(900)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-02-handsup")
        # a fifth press must leave slide 2
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(200)
        assert page.evaluate("location.hash") == "#3", page.evaluate("location.hash")

        # slide 3: two-beat marvin
        goto(page, 3)
        page.wait_for_timeout(2400 + 500)
        s1 = marvin_state(page)
        page.wait_for_timeout(2600)
        s2 = marvin_state(page)
        print("slide3 beats:", s1, s2)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-03-marvin-beat2")

        # slide 4: terminal callback, full replay + marvin
        goto(page, 4)
        page.wait_for_timeout(6200)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-04-forgot")
        page.wait_for_timeout(2400)
        print("slide4 marvin:", marvin_state(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-04-forgot-marvin2")

        # slide 5: why fragment
        goto(page, 5)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1200)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(900)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-05-git-why")

        # slide 6: shrug mood
        goto(page, 6)
        page.wait_for_timeout(3200 + 500)
        print("slide6 marvin:", marvin_state(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-06-shrug")

        # slide 10: sleepy
        goto(page, 10)
        page.wait_for_timeout(2600 + 500)
        print("slide10 marvin:", marvin_state(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-10-sleepy")

        # slide 11: three fragments
        goto(page, 11)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        for _ in range(3):
            page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(200)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1400)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-11-not")

        # slide 12: wifi line
        goto(page, 12)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1400)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-12-demo")

        # slide 16: friday fragment
        goto(page, 16)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(2200)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-16-friday")

        # slide 20: heart
        goto(page, 20)
        page.wait_for_timeout(2600 + 500)
        print("slide20 marvin:", marvin_state(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-20-heart")

        # slide 21: party on, then off, then slide-change teardown
        goto(page, 21)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        page.keyboard.press("m"); page.wait_for_timeout(1800)
        print("party:", page.evaluate("({party: document.body.classList.contains('party'), visors: document.querySelectorAll('#party .party-visor').length})"), marvin_state(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-21-party")
        page.keyboard.press("m"); page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        print("party off:", page.evaluate("({party: document.body.classList.contains('party'), box: !!document.getElementById('party')})"))
        page.keyboard.press("m"); page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowLeft"); page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        print("party after slidechange:", page.evaluate("({party: document.body.classList.contains('party'), box: !!document.getElementById('party')})"))
        # cameo on slide 20 should still be scheduled after teardown
        page.wait_for_timeout(2600 + 500)
        print("slide20 cameo survives teardown:", marvin_state(page))

        # cameo cancels cleanly when leaving mid-beat
        goto(page, 3); page.wait_for_timeout(2600)
        goto(page, 7); page.wait_for_timeout(3500)
        print("slide7 (no cue) after leaving slide 3 mid-cameo:", marvin_state(page))

        print("errors:", errors)
        browser.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run(1920, 1080, "hd")
    run(1366, 768, "sm")

Yes, there's room, but the deck is timed for 30 to 40 minutes, so I'd cap it at two or three inserts. Each full slide costs roughly a minute of stage time. Here are the options, ordered by where they'd sit in the deck.

**Act 1 · The developer problem**

1. **The receipt.** After slide 4. A long CVS-style receipt that types itself out: "we use pnpm, not npm ×14", "tests live in /spec ×22", "don't touch the migrations ×9", "yes, Redis is in cluster mode ×31". Total at the bottom: "3h 40m of re-explaining · roughly one Silk Board crossing." Ties the pain to a number the room feels. Strongest Act 1 option.

2. **Five stages of agent grief.** After slide 4 or 6. Five click-reveal stages: Denial ("it's in the context window somewhere"), Anger ("I TOLD you about the cluster"), Bargaining ("just read CLAUDE.md first, please"), Depression (pasting the same 400-word prompt for the ninth time), Acceptance (points at this deck). Familiar format, easy laugh, slightly generic.

3. **A brief history of remembering things.** Before slide 5. A timeline: cave paintings, sticky notes, git commit, then a coding agent saying "Sure! What are we working on?" Sets up "Git stores the result" nicely but overlaps with slide 4's joke.

**Act 2 · Entire today**

4. **Post-demo hedge slide.** Right after the demo. Two halves: "If that worked: this is what versioned context looks like." and "If it didn't: this is exactly why we version the context." You win either way, and the room knows you planned for the wifi. Cheap insurance and a real laugh if the demo wobbles.

5. **Marvin's performance review.** After slide 10. A mock HR card. Strengths: "remembers everything now." Areas for growth: "still thinks he's the best engineer in the room." Manager comment: "swalpa adjust maadi." Cute, but the weakest fit with the product story.

**Act 3 · The developer harness**

6. **Meanwhile, at a startup in Koramangala.** Right after the Act 3 divider. A fake WhatsApp group thread. PM: "can we ship today?" Dev: "it's 5pm on a Friday." Agent: "Done! Merged to main 😊". Dev: "..." This is the setup that makes slide 16's friday-5pm runner and Gates land twice as hard. Strongest Act 3 option.

7. **Bengaluru vs. your agent.** A comparison table. Traffic: never forgets to be jammed. Agent: forgets everything. Weather: unpredictable. Agent: predictably amnesiac. Auto driver: "meter mele 20." Agent: "context mele 100k tokens." Very local, very shareable, but table-shaped humor is slower on stage.

**The invitation**

8. **This talk, as a Checkpoint.** Before slide 20. A Checkpoint card for the talk itself: "prompt: make Bengaluru laugh · 34 tool calls · 2 corrections (wifi) · constraint found: 40 minutes · attempt 1: rejected by demo gods · handoff: you." Meta, on-brand, and it turns the product into the punchline. My favourite of the set.

**My recommendation:** the receipt (1), the Koramangala thread (6), and the talk-as-Checkpoint (8). One per act, each doing setup work for a serious slide that follows. Add the post-demo hedge (4) only if you're nervous about the wifi. That's three or four minutes of stage time, which fits a 40-minute slot but would squeeze a 30-minute one.

- **Ghajini · "Your agent has 15-minute memory."** A wall of Polaroids pinned like Sanjay's: "REDIS IS CLUSTER MODE. NO LUA." "KEEP THE TOKEN BUCKET." "a3f9c12 · THIS WAS ME." Punch: "Sanjay had tattoos. Your agent has a context window." Marvin: "kalpana? ...i mean, checkpoint." Bridges straight into Act 2.
- **Sholay · "Kitne agents the?"** Gabbar's interrogation as a terminal. "Paanch, sardar." "Paanch agents... aur context ek bhi nahi?" Ends with "Ab tera kya hoga, context?" Pairs with slide 6's fragmentation.
- **Hera Pheri · "Hello, kaun?"** Baburao answering the phone is Agent B opening a new session. Funny, but it duplicates slide 4's joke.
- **Andaz Apna Apna · Crime Master Gogo.** "Aaya hoon, kuch toh loot ke jaunga" as the agent vendor walking off with your history. Sharp answer to "who owns your history?"

**Act 2 · Entire today**

- **Deewaar · "Mere paas Checkpoint hai."** Two terminals face off. Agent A lists everything it has: 34 tool calls, 6 test suites, 42 green tests, the commit. Agent B, running Entire, replies with one line. The whole room says it with you. Strongest option on the list.
- **Bahubali · "Kattappa ne Bahubali ko kyun maara?"** India waited two years for a "why". Your codebase asks it about every line. `entire explain` answers in two seconds. Telugu, not Bollywood, but Bengaluru will roar.

- **3 Idiots · "Aal izz well."** Pre-demo slide. The six demo steps with a heart-tap ritual. Tension release right before the wifi test.

- **Mr. India · "Mogambo khush hua."** The Gate verdict slide. All runners pass, a giant stamp lands: MOGAMBO KHUSH HUA · merge allowed. Fail one and Mogambo is not khush.
- **DDLJ · "Ja PR ja, merge ho ja."** Bauji letting go is the Gate approving. Bonus: "Palat... palat... palat" for `entire blame`.
- **Om Shanti Om · "Picture abhi baaki hai mere dost."** The roadmap slide. Agents reborn every session with no memory of a past life, until now. Fits the Act 3 divider.

"""Verify the three Bollywood interval slides + CTA one-liner + party on the new close index."""
import os
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

OUT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "shots2")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
BASE = "http://localhost:8123/index.html"

def shoot(page, name):
    page.screenshot(path=os.path.join(OUT, name + ".png"))

def goto(page, n):
    page.goto(f"{BASE}#{n}")
    page.wait_for_timeout(300)

def marvin(page):
    return page.evaluate("""() => { const h = document.getElementById('marvinHud');
      return {on: h.classList.contains('is-on'), mood: h.dataset.mood, line: h.querySelector('.marvin-say').textContent}; }""")

def run(width, height, tag):
    with sync_playwright() as p:
        browser = p.chromium.launch(channel="msedge", headless=True)
        page = browser.new_page(viewport={"width": width, "height": height})
        errors = []
        page.on("pageerror", lambda e: errors.append(str(e)))
        page.on("console", lambda m: errors.append(m.text) if m.type == "error" else None)

        total = page.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll('.slide').length") if False else None
        goto(page, 1)
        total = page.evaluate("document.querySelectorAll('.slide').length")
        print("slides:", total)

        # 5 · Ghajini
        goto(page, 5)
        page.wait_for_timeout(2000)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-05-ghajini-wall")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(700)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-05-ghajini-checkpoint")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(900)
        # rotation must survive the reveal
        rot = page.evaluate("getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.polaroid.is-checkpoint')).transform")
        print("checkpoint polaroid transform:", rot)
        page.wait_for_timeout(3600)
        print("ghajini marvin:", marvin(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-05-ghajini-punch")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(200)
        assert page.evaluate("location.hash") == "#6", page.evaluate("location.hash")

        # 10 · Deewaar
        goto(page, 10)
        page.wait_for_timeout(4900)
        hidden = page.evaluate("getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.deewaar-line')).opacity")
        print("deewaar line opacity before click (expect 0):", hidden)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-10-deewaar-speech")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(800)
        shown = page.evaluate("getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.deewaar-line')).opacity")
        print("deewaar line opacity after click (expect 1):", shown)
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(900)
        print("deewaar marvin:", marvin(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-10-deewaar-punch")

        # 19 · Mogambo
        goto(page, 19)
        page.wait_for_timeout(3400)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-19-mogambo-runners")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(700)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-19-mogambo-stamp")
        page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight"); page.wait_for_timeout(900)
        print("mogambo marvin:", marvin(page))
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-19-mogambo-foot")

        # 22 · CTA one-liner
        goto(page, 22)
        page.wait_for_timeout(4800)
        shoot(page, f"{tag}-22-cta")

        # 24 · party still works on the close slide
        goto(page, 24)
        page.wait_for_timeout(1200)
        page.keyboard.press("m"); page.wait_for_timeout(1500)
        print("party:", page.evaluate("({party: document.body.classList.contains('party'), visors: document.querySelectorAll('#party .party-visor').length})"))
        page.keyboard.press("m")

        print("errors:", errors)
        browser.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run(1920, 1080, "hd")
    run(1366, 768, "sm")
